loughton.s1_head: Kitting the events trade of the Epping Forest fringe
s1loc: Loughton anchors the Epping Forest events scene. Lopping Hall on the High Road, opened in 1884 and gifted by the Corporation of London, runs its stage for the Loughton Amateur Dramatic Society and the Loughton Operatic Society, while the National Jazz Archive based in the town puts on performances across the district. Out in the forest itself, ancient glades and open spaces host fairs, fun runs and open-air events that fill the warmer months around Loughton and Buckhurst Hill.

And the trade runs at every size. Major venues, festival operators and production companies across this corner of Essex field large seasonal crews and buy through procurement, while independent event crews, promoters and entertainers around Loughton and Debden need just a few branded pieces. A workwear supplier here has to serve the busy hall production and the single crew alike, which is why we run trade accounts and direct online ordering side by side.

The wider catchment counts too. The Epping Forest Festival and similar district celebrations draw stewards, stage and crew teams out across the green spaces, town-centre markets and church-hall events keep their own grassroots calendars going, and dance schools and exercise groups rehearse and perform at Lopping Hall year round. From a hall pantomime to a forest-edge fair or a jazz night, the same crews need branded, hard-wearing kit through the season.
